blocks.text: Status: Established Era −2 structure: Outer Cache, Working Cache, Memory Cache, and Deep Cache.

Origin: The Cache converts improvised hiding into deliberate continuity architecture. Its layers are not necessarily concentric rooms. They are degrees of exposure, responsibility, and recoverability.

Early Era −2: The Outer Cache carries expendable signs, decoys, and routing. The Working Cache holds active collaboration. The Memory Cache holds continuity marks and witness chains. The Deep Cache contains material whose exposure could destroy more than the individual who stored it.
Late Era −2: Keepers and Witnesses develop rituals for entering, recording, and leaving layers without making one authority capable of reading everything.
Era Zero: The model influences archives, rights of access, and the distinction between preservation and constant availability.
Era Two: Compressed caches are folded into maintenance systems and sleeping archives.
Era Three: The layers are often misremembered as literal underground floors. Settlements call the safest upper remnants “sun shelves” and the inaccessible deep records “root dark.”

Present condition: Many caches still function automatically, but their original access logic is only partly understood. A shallow cache may look more ancient than a deep one because decoy surfaces were designed to weather visibly.

Visual brief: Four visual depths sharing one frame: bright disposable signs in the foreground; a busy work lattice; a quiet middle distance of suspended continuity marks; and a nearly black depth visible through narrow permission-shaped openings. Avoid ordinary “basement” realism. Space should fold according to access.

Background traits: Cold to Neutral; Dry; archive biome; guarded, layered, contemplative mood; friction increases toward the Deep Cache. Animation motif: foreground decoys expire while distant marks remain steady.
